chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar told us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom.
Who are the Aal (Family)? He said: His offspring, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his Family). I said: And who are the Ahl (People)? He said: The Imams (peace be upon them).
I said: His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Enter, (O) Family of Pharaoh, into the most severe punishment.'
He said: By Allah, he did not mean other than his daughter.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Aal of Pharaoh' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* establishes a hierarchical distinction in Quranic terminology, defining the Prophet's 'Aal' as his progeny and the 'Ahl' specifically as the Imams, thereby anchoring the concept of *Ahl al-Bayt* in divine lineage. The Imam’s interpretation of 'Aal Pharaoh' as his daughter demonstrates the semantic flexibility of the term, which can refer to a specific individual or a close lineage rather than a broad collective, a nuance critical to Shia exegetical tradition. This hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the exclusive status of the Imams as the true 'People' associated with the Prophet.
